facts.statement: Chaoyangopterus fossils were discovered in the Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation near Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Chaoyangopterus was found in rocks dating back to the Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Dapingfang, Chaoyang.

facts.statement: The genus Chaoyangopterus was named and described in 2003 by Wang Xiaolin and Zhou Zhonghe.
facts.quote: Chaoyangopterus was named and described in 2003 by Wang Xiaolin and Zhou Zhonghe.

facts.statement: The species name 'zhangi' honors journalist Zhang Wanlian for his work protecting fossil sites.
facts.quote: The specific name honors journalist Zhang Wanlian for his efforts in protecting fossil sites.

facts.statement: Chaoyangopterus had a toothless skull approximately 270 mm long and an estimated wingspan of 1.85 meters.
facts.quote: The skull is about 270 mm long and toothless, and its wingspan is estimated to have been around 1.85 m.

facts.statement: The original describers classified Chaoyangopterus as a nyctosaurid, noting it was most similar to Nyctosaurus.
facts.quote: Wang and Zhou concluded that it compared most closely to Nyctosaurus and classified it as a nyctosaurid

facts.statement: David Unwin classified Chaoyangopterus within the Tapejaridae family, a group of azhdarchoids known for large head crests.
facts.quote: David Unwin, in a popular work, included it without comment with the tapejarid family of azhdarchoid pterosaurs, known for their large head crests.

facts.statement: A 2006 analysis by Lü Junchang and Ji Qiang identified Chaoyangopterus as a basal azhdarchoid without specific familial affiliation.
facts.quote: A detailed phylogenetic analysis of Liaoning pterosaurs published by Lü Junchang and Ji Qiang in 2006 found it instead to be a basal azhdarchoid of no particular familial affiliation.

facts.statement: Later analysis by Lü and Unwin placed Chaoyangopterus in the family Chaoyangopteridae, a clade including Jidapterus and Shenzhoupterus.
facts.quote: subsequent analysis by Lü and Unwin found that within the Azhdarchoidea it formed a clade with several other forms such as Jidapterus and Shenzhoupterus, which they named Chaoyangopteridae.

facts.statement: In 2006, Wang and Zhou argued that Chaoyangopterus belonged to the Pteranodontidae family and that other genera were junior synonyms.
facts.quote: Wang and Zhou, however, stated in 2006 that Chaoyangopterus was a member of the Pteranodontidae and that Jidapterus, Eoazhdarcho and Eopteranodon are subjective junior synonyms of the former.

facts.statement: A 2017 redescription of Jidapterus refuted the claim that Chaoyangopterus and related genera were synonyms.
facts.quote: This interpretation was not supported by a 2017 redescription of Jidapterus, which was able to reliably distinguish all of these genera.

facts.statement: A 2011 study by Pinheiro et al. placed Chaoyangopterus in the subfamily Chaoyangopterinae within the family Tapejaridae.
facts.quote: The one on the left is a topology by Felipe Pinheiro and colleagues in 2011, they recovered Chaoyangopterus within the family Tapejaridae, more specifically within a subfamily called Chaoyangopterinae, sister taxon to both Jidapterus and Shenzhoupterus.

facts.statement: Wang originally assumed the toothless Chaoyangopterus was a fish-eater, though its full paleobiology remains undetailed.
facts.quote: Chaoyangopterus is known to have been a toothless pterosaur and was assumed by Wang to have been a piscivore or fish-eater, but other relevant details of its paleobiology will have to await a more detailed description.

facts.statement: Chaoyangopterus lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
